claim.claim-text: 2. The method of claim 1, wherein determining, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A), and based on a comparison of the first audio input quality and the second audio input quality by the negotiation module (40) of the first computing device (2A), whether the first computing device (2A) should process the spoken audio input comprises: determining which of the first and second computing devices has a highest level of audio input quality.
3. The method of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the audio input quality comprises a volume of the spoken audio input.
4. The method of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the audio input quality comprises a strength of the spoken audio input in decibels.
5. The method of any preceding claim, wherein the audio input quality comprises a signal-to-noise ratio of the spoken audio input.
6. The method of any one of claims 1-5, further comprising:

sending, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A) and to the negotiation module of the second computing device (2B), an indication of a type of the first computing device (2A); and receiving, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A) and from the negotiation module of the second computing device (2B), an indication of a type of the second computing device (2B), wherein determining, by the negotiation module of the first computing device, whether the first computing device (2A) should process the spoken audio input is further based at least in part on the type of the first computing device (2A) and the type of the second computing device (2B).

7. The method of claim 6, wherein determining, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A), whether the first computing device (2A) should process the spoken audio input comprises determining which of the first and second computing devices is of a type having the highest device priority level.

8. The method of any one of claims 1-7, further comprising: responsive to determining that the first computing device (2A) should process the spoken audio input, ceasing, by the first computing device (2A), temporarily deactivating, by the first computing device (2A), an audio monitoring module.
9. The method of claim any of claims 1-8, wherein the spoken audio input is also received by a third computing device (2C) of the plurality of computing devices (2), the method further comprising:

sending, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A) and to a negotiation module of the third computing device (2C), the indication of the first audio input quality; and receiving, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A) and from the negotiation module of the third computing device (2C), an indication of a third audio input quality of the spoken audio input received by the third computing device (2C); and determining, by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A), and based on a comparison of the first audio input quality and the second audio input quality and the third audio input quality by the negotiation module of the first computing device (2A), whether the first computing device (2A) should process the spoken audio input.
10. The method of any of claims 1-9, wherein the spoken audio input is also received by each other computing device (2C) of the plurality of computing devices (2), the method further comprising:
11. The method of claim 1, further comprising: executing, by the first computing device (2A), a spoken command included in the spoken audio input.
at least one processor; and a memory comprising instructions that, when executed by the at least one processor, cause the at least one processor to perform the method of any one of claims 1-11.

13. A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium encoded with instructions that, when executed, cause at least one processor of a first computing device (2A) to perform the method of any one of claims 1-11.
